toegepas.voor: en dan swel dit dikker op
toegepas.na: en dan swel dit op en word dikker
toegepas.rede_vinder: 'swel dikker op' is an awkward combination, because 'opswel' already means growing bigger; splitting it keeps both ideas and reads naturally.
toegepas.fout: 'swel dikker op' is an unusual, slightly pleonastic combination of the separable verb with a comparative wedged inside it.
toegepas.rede_keurder: The proposal keeps 'dikker' as the plain-word gloss of 'swel', reads naturally, and says the same thing in the same order.

toegepas.voor: Kyk na 'n plant in 'n pot met blare aan sy stam
toegepas.na: Kyk na 'n potplant met blare aan sy stam
toegepas.rede_vinder: As written, 'met blare aan sy stam' can attach to 'pot'; 'potplant', the word the lesson uses later, removes the ambiguity.
toegepas.fout: 'in 'n pot met blare aan sy stam' lets the phrase attach to 'pot' on a first reading, a small stumble.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'potplant' is the lesson's own later word, removes the stumble, is shorter and keeps the meaning.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: Two attributive adjectives before a noun read more naturally separated by a comma than joined by 'en', especially straight after the list 'lank, dun en swak'.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'klein en bleek blaartjies' is natural Afrikaans, so the comma form is a lateral move.

laat_vaar.voor: Watter saad dink jy ontkiem eerste?
laat_vaar.na: Watter saad, dink jy, ontkiem eerste?
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'dink jy' is an inserted clause here and is set off by commas, which also keeps the reader from reading 'saad dink' together.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'Watter saad dink jy ontkiem eerste?' is the normal Afrikaans question with 'dink jy' as the main clause, not an inserted one, so the commas are optional and add nothing.

vlae.teks: Later druk 'n klein stingel boontoe by die saad uit.
vlae.rede: The lesson calls this part 'stam' everywhere else (including the measuring list, 'die hoogte van die stam'); 'stingel' here may read as a different part to a Grade 4 learner. Not changed because it is a subject term and the choice is the writer's.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: maak baie maklik wortels op hierdie manier
laat_vaar_vorige.na: maak op hierdie manier baie maklik wortels
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: In Afrikaans the adverbial of manner sits more naturally before the object than trailing at the end.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The original word order reads naturally; moving the adverbial is a lateral move.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'voor hom gegroei' (grew before it, the seed) reads awkwardly and 'hom' for the seed clashes with 'dit' elsewhere; 'al voorheen' keeps the meaning.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'al voorheen' loses the relation 'before it (the seed)' and is vaguer, while the original is correct Afrikaans.

laat_vaar_vorige.blok: Wat om te meet en aan te teken
laat_vaar_vorige.voor: Tel hoeveel blare die plantjie elke week het.
laat_vaar_vorige.na: Tel elke week hoeveel blare die plantjie het.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'elke week' belongs with the instruction 'tel' (count weekly), not inside the counted clause.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The original is natural Afrikaans and already means counting the leaves each week; the reorder is lateral.
